# State Class View (variant): Environmental review specialist (local)

> **Not a classification basis / not a job analysis / not for RIF or rating decisions.**
>
> Task importance, time share, critical and needed-at-entry values are agent drafts (raterType llm, validationStatus draft, evidence S): assessment pending (job analysis). They are not job-analysis results and no human has reviewed them. Target levels are editorial design drafts. A credential gate is shown only when its issuer is verified with a cited source; the other gates are counted, not shown, until the issuer is verified (CR-CP-001 C7).

- **Role:** Environmental review specialist (`seed:R10-environmental-review-specialist`, P1); authority position (editorial): regulator
- **Generated:** pipelines/views/state_class_view.py@0.2.0, rule state-class-view@0.1.0 (registered rule, status active), as of 2026-10-23

## Mapped classes

No class is mapped in the pilot jurisdictions (TX, WA and PA (state), Lewis County WA (county environmental health), Philadelphia Water Department (municipal utility)). The role's targets below are what a jurisdiction would crosswalk its own class specification against.

## Competency targets by role level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)

- Conduct environmental impact review of proposed actions — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Select, justify and document the appropriate level of environmental review — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Build and maintain a defensible administrative record — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Direct and evaluate applicant- or contractor-prepared environmental documents — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Coordinate lead, cooperating and participating agencies to a shared schedule — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Assess effects on protected species and conduct interagency consultation on proposed actions — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Review effects of proposed actions on historic properties and resolve them through consultation — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Assess litigation exposure and design decisions for resilience on remand — senior L3, lead L4
- Analyze regulatory, planning and public-comment text at scale with traceable citations — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Analyze cumulative burdens and distributional effects of environmental decisions — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Design proportionate public engagement when participation is discretionary — journey L2, senior L2, lead L3
- Identify and analyze the parties affected by or interested in a decision — journey L2, senior L2, lead L3
- Quantify and communicate uncertainty for environmental decisions — journey L2, senior L2, lead L3
- Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty — journey L2, senior L2, lead L2
- Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary — journey L2, senior L2, lead L3
- Maintain the integrity of regulatory and scientific findings under institutional pressure — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Supervise staff and volunteers in environmental work — senior L3, lead L4
- Practise cultural humility in community, field and team work — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Design accessible, inclusive public engagement and services — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Build working partnerships with communities affected by environmental decisions — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
